root.label: US Supreme Court lifts stay in Christa Pike execution

events.label: US Supreme Court lifts stay in Christa Pike execution

slots.name: dissenting justices
slots.sentence: It came over the dissent of the three liberal justices.

slots.name: Pike age
slots.sentence: Pike, 50, was set to be executed by lethal injection at 10 a.m. local time at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.

slots.name: conviction year
slots.sentence: Pike was convicted of first-degree murder in 1996 for killing 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a fellow Jobs Corps Center worker from Knoxville, in an apparent jealous rage.

slots.name: age at murder
slots.sentence: Pike described herself in a state clemency petition as a “mentally ill 18-year-old kid” when the murder took place.

slots.name: execution authorization
slots.sentence: The Supreme Court lifted that order hours later at Tennessee’s request.

slots.name: women on death row
slots.sentence: She is the lone woman on the state’s death row.

slots.name: stay status
slots.sentence: the U.S. Supreme Court overturned that stay hours later to clear the way for her to be put to death.
